Estimate Non-wear from Raw Accelerometry with the GGIR Method

Source: R/acti_calculate_wear_raw_ggir.R
acti_calculate_wear_raw_ggir.Rd

Detects non-wear and signal clipping from raw tri-axial acceleration with the algorithm in GGIR (van Hees et al. 2011, 2013), as implemented in GGIR's detect_nonwear_clipping() and g.weardec(). This is a standalone port and does not require GGIR. Usually called through acti_calculate_wear_raw().

Usage

acti_calculate_wear_raw_ggir(
  data,
  sample_rate = NULL,
  medium_epoch = 900,
  long_epoch = 3600,
  approach = c("2023", "2013"),
  sd_threshold = 0.013,
  range_threshold = 0.15,
  dynamic_range = NULL,
  clip_threshold = NULL,
  wear_threshold = 2,
  clipping_threshold = 0.3,
  edge_correction = TRUE,
  filter_max_hours = NULL,
  filter_window = NULL,
  align_start = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame of raw accelerometer data with a time column and X, Y, Z columns, or an AccData object. Data should be calibrated (e.g. with acti_calibrate()) and regularly sampled.

sample_rate

Sampling frequency (Hz). If NULL, taken from the sample_rate attribute of data.

medium_epoch

Length, in seconds, of the epoch the output is reported in (GGIR windowsizes[2]).

long_epoch

Length, in seconds, of the window used to evaluate non-wear (GGIR windowsizes[3]).

approach

Non-wear window approach (GGIR nonwear_approach). "2023" (GGIR default) uses a forward-looking long window, evaluated on a subsample of ceiling(sample_rate / 5), and labels every medium epoch it covers. "2013" uses a long window centred on each medium epoch and labels only that epoch.

sd_threshold

Standard deviation (g) below which an axis is considered still. GGIR uses 0.013, or 1.2 * rmc.noise for ad-hoc formats.

range_threshold

Range (g) below which an axis is considered still (GGIR nonwear_range_threshold, in mg, divided by 1000). GGIR uses 0.15, or 0.2 for Verisense devices.

dynamic_range

Dynamic range of the device (g), e.g. c(-8, 8). If NULL, it is taken from the attributes or header of data when available. Used to set clip_threshold.

clip_threshold

Absolute acceleration (g) above which a sample is counted as clipped. Defaults to the dynamic range minus 0.5, or 7.5 when the dynamic range is unknown, as in GGIR.

wear_threshold

Minimum number of axes that must be still for an epoch to be non-wear. Fixed at 2 in GGIR.

clipping_threshold

Fraction of clipped samples above which an epoch is flagged as clipping. Fixed at 0.3 in GGIR.

edge_correction

Should non-wear starting (ending) within the first (last) 3 hours of the recording be extended to the start (end)? GGIR nonWearEdgeCorrection.

filter_max_hours, filter_window

If filter_max_hours is not NULL, non-wear bouts shorter than filter_max_hours hours occurring inside the clock window filter_window = c(start_hour, end_hour) are relabelled as wear (GGIR nonwearFiltermaxHours and nonwearFilterWindow). The window may wrap midnight, e.g. c(22, 7).

align_start

Should samples before the first clock time aligned to medium_epoch be dropped, as GGIR does? If FALSE, epochs start at the first sample.

Value

A tibble with one row per medium epoch:

time

Start of the epoch.

nonwear_score

Number of axes (0–3) meeting the non-wear criteria (GGIR nonwearscore).

clipping_score

Maximum fraction of clipped samples across axes (GGIR clippingscore).

nonwear

Non-wear from the score (GGIR r1).

clipping

Clipping (GGIR r2).

nonwear_additional

Additional non-wear from the bout rules (GGIR r3).

wear

TRUE if none of nonwear, clipping, or nonwear_additional is flagged.

Details

For each medium epoch (default 15 minutes), a long window (default 60 minutes) is evaluated per axis. An axis is scored as non-wear when both its standard deviation is below sd_threshold and its range is below range_threshold. The non-wear score is the number of axes (0–3) that meet both criteria, and an epoch is non-wear when the score is at least wear_threshold. An epoch is clipped when more than clipping_threshold of its samples on any axis exceed clip_threshold (or, if any sample exceeds 1.5 * clip_threshold, the whole epoch is clipped). Short wear bouts surrounded by long non-wear bouts are then relabelled as non-wear, following GGIR part 2.

GGIR reads files in chunks (24 hours for GT3X files) and scores each chunk separately. With approach = "2023", a window that starts in one chunk cannot label epochs in the next, so GGIR's nonwearscore can be lower for the first epochs after a chunk boundary. This function scores the whole recording at once. GGIR also imputes time gaps before scoring; this function does not.

References

van Hees VT, et al. (2011). Estimation of daily energy expenditure in pregnant and non-pregnant women using a wrist-worn tri-axial accelerometer. PLoS ONE 6(7): e22922. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0022922

van Hees VT, et al. (2013). Separating movement and gravity components in an acceleration signal and implications for the assessment of human daily physical activity. PLoS ONE 8(4): e61691. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0061691

See also

acti_calculate_wear_raw(), acti_calculate_wear_raw_actipy()

Examples

n = 3 * 3600 * 10
time = as.POSIXct("2020-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC") + (seq_len(n) - 1) / 10
moving = rep(c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE), each = n / 3)
set.seed(1)
data = data.frame(
  time = time,
  X = ifelse(moving, stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), 0),
  Y = ifelse(moving, stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), 0),
  Z = ifelse(moving, stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), 1)
)
acti_calculate_wear_raw_ggir(data, sample_rate = 10)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 7
#>    time                nonwear_score clipping_score nonwear clipping
#>    <dttm>                      <dbl>          <dbl> <lgl>   <lgl>   
#>  1 2020-01-01 00:00:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#>  2 2020-01-01 00:15:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#>  3 2020-01-01 00:30:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#>  4 2020-01-01 00:45:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#>  5 2020-01-01 01:00:00             3              0 TRUE    FALSE   
#>  6 2020-01-01 01:15:00             3              0 TRUE    FALSE   
#>  7 2020-01-01 01:30:00             3              0 TRUE    FALSE   
#>  8 2020-01-01 01:45:00             3              0 TRUE    FALSE   
#>  9 2020-01-01 02:00:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#> 10 2020-01-01 02:15:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#> 11 2020-01-01 02:30:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#> 12 2020-01-01 02:45:00             0              0 FALSE   FALSE   
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: nonwear_additional <lgl>, wear <lgl>
